about.text: Whey with much of its lactose and minerals filtered out through an ultrafiltration membrane that holds back the proteins, then dried: a powder of 35 to 80 % protein in its dry matter. Used in sports and clinical nutrition and in many foods.

how.text: The membrane lets water, lactose and minerals through and holds the proteins, so the retentate gets richer in protein the harder it is concentrated. WPC80 needs diafiltration; WPI (above 90 %) goes further.

steps.name: separate
steps.note: Whey is defatted and clarified, fat and casein fines removed; microfiltration is an option.

steps.name: ultrafilter
steps.note: The membrane holds back the protein.

steps.name: diafilter
steps.note: Water added during UF to wash out more lactose and minerals.

facts.v: More than 99 % of the true protein
Concentrated to about 9 % dry matter (35 % protein) before drying
UF retentate taken to 27–32 % solids; example 81.0 % crude protein, 3.5 % lactose
